content.text: All redlines validated. Submitting findings for all 18 rules.

input.quote: the amount of any other actual direct damages, up to the greater of $100,000 or the charges paid by Customer to IBM for the Services in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the accrual of the first claim related to the Services.
input.rationale: The caps are mutual and based on 12 months' charges (greater of $100,000), and indemnity payments and bodily injury/property damage sit outside the cap; consequential damages are mutually excluded with our payment obligations properly carved out. However, there is no carve-out for breach of confidentiality/data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and § 9.1(c)(2) excludes IBM liability entirely for loss of or damage to our records or data in a hosting deal — that fails the fallback on carve-outs. Redline adds a mutual carve-out sentence and deletes the data-loss exclusion; indemnities and confidentiality must sit outside the cap.

input.quote: If a third party claims or threatens a claim that Materials or Base Components IBM provides to Customer or uses in connection with the performance of the Services infringe that party's patent, trademark, copyright, or trade secret, then IBM will indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Customer, its Enterprise and their respective employees, officers, agents and directors against that claim
input.rationale: IBM gives a defend-and-indemnify IP infringement indemnity covering patent, trademark, copyright and trade secret, with the usual exclusions (our contributions, modifications, combinations, non-IBM items) and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and indemnity payments are uncapped under § 9.1(a) — this sits at (indeed above) the fallback. Noted, not flagged: no indemnity for IBM's breach of law, data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and our reverse indemnity at § 8.2(a)(3) for Services Recipient claims "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services" is broader than our preferred narrow scope; we would raise both as secondary asks.
